label: Northwestern EDI · Team project
title: Squad Up
proposition: A shared ordering concept that lets a group join, choose, pay, and get ready without one person managing everyone.
context: A group order starts before checkout. People are still arriving, changing plans, choosing food, and figuring out who owes what.
role: User research · Journey design · Interaction architecture · Prototyping

hero.alt: McDonald’s Squad Up interface showing live participant progress
hero.caption: Live bag states show who has joined, who is choosing, and when the group is ready.

sections.title: The order starts before checkout
sections.intro: Across 4 observations, 8 interviews, and 22 survey responses, we saw McDonald’s as a stop between other activities. The order had to preserve social momentum, not become a separate administrative task.

notes.text: The order is part of the hangout, not a separate task.

visuals.alt: McDonald’s research sample showing four site observations, eight interviews, and twenty-two survey responses
visuals.caption: The project began with four observations, eight interviews, and twenty-two survey responses.

visuals.alt: Research quote about McDonald’s fitting into an after-class routine
visuals.caption: An after-class routine showed how ordering competes with time, travel, and social momentum.

sections.title: One person becomes the coordinator
sections.intro: Existing paths create an awkward tradeoff: one person collects everyone’s choices and chases payment, or people pay separately and lose a shared view of the order.

notes.text: One person coordinates the food, or everyone coordinates payment.
Group visibility and payment clarity have to improve together.

visuals.alt: Comparison of group ordering through one payer versus individual orders and payment chasing
visuals.caption: Current options split coordination and payment instead of solving both for the group.

visuals.alt: Teen group-ordering problem landscape and needs
visuals.caption: Teen needs connected easy ordering with social reinforcement, financial clarity, and familiar behavior.

sections.title: One order, individual agency
sections.intro: We reframed the opportunity as synchronized participation: one shared order, while each person keeps ownership of their choices and payment.

visuals.alt: Opportunity brief for a synchronized multi-user McDonald’s order
visuals.caption: The first concept tested synchronized carts, clearer coordination, and the risk of added setup.

visuals.alt: Squad Up value propositions for payment, pickup, and customization
visuals.caption: Customization, payment, and pickup became the three value checks for the shared order.

sections.title: From invite to pickup
sections.intro: The concept connects invitation, joining, individual bags, payment, readiness, and pickup as one visible group state. Kiosk, app, web, and assisted entry points all converge on the same order.

sections.title: What I took forward
sections.intro: Squad Up reinforced that group experiences need more than collaboration features. The product has to show ownership, progress, and intervention clearly enough that coordination feels lighter instead of merely moving into a new interface.

closingContext: Student team project created at Northwestern EDI using McDonald’s ordering as the design context; not affiliated with or shipped by McDonald’s.
